Jeremiah 6:16 explicitly equates the good way with something Israel must “walk” in, and refusal of that way is refusal to walk accordingly. Matthew 7:14 contrasts two ways by their conduct-associated destinations and fits the established biblical Two Ways pattern. Genesis 18:19 further defines “the way of the LORD” as doing justice and judgment, while 2 Peter 2:21 associates the way of righteousness with the holy commandment. The strongest christological counter-reading rightly explains John 14:6 and Hebrews 10:19–20 as identifying Jesus personally as access to the Father, but it does not explain the entry’s actual proof texts better. Nor does it exclude the book’s core: the chapter explicitly presents Jesus as the perfect personal embodiment of the covenant way.
